memos.scout:
Case for buying Ponzi now, from the brief alone:

Demand looks broad and recent. The last 15 minutes show 736 buyers against 530 sellers, with 351.76 SOL bought versus 311.88 sold and net inflow of 39.87 SOL. Price is up 26% over 30 minutes and 126% over the last 15, so it has not stalled. Concentration is low: top-3 holders hold 6.2% and the top-5 early buyers account for 12.2% of early buys, with no airdrop dump seen. The class is ORGANIC, not factory or operator-backed, and it is 17.7% off its 30-minute high, a modest pullback rather than a collapse.

The weak points are real. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes was 1.14, the bundle share is 20%, and pool depth is thin at 96 SOL, so round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% take a real bite. Against a base rate of roughly 20% losses per random buy, the case rests on the recent net inflow continuing, which the brief cannot confirm. Honest read: a tentative case exists, but it is thin enough that skipping is defensible.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss here is a dip-and-fade after the momentum run. The coin is up 26% over 30 minutes and 126% in the last 15, but it has already pulled back 17.7% from its high, and 530 sellers against 736 buyers in the last 15 minutes shows the crowd is already exiting. Sell-to-buy ratio of 1.14 in the first two minutes after graduation and a launch bot present suggest early liquidity was rotating out, not building. Pool depth is only 96 SOL, so a $20 round trip faces 1.4-5.1% in costs before any move, and a shallow book can gap down hard on a single large sell. The name "Ponzi" is itself a warning sign, though it is creator-chosen data and proves nothing alone. Bundle share of 20% and top-3 concentration of 6% look moderate, but the decay pattern argues skip.
